note: Every circuit that has held a World Championship round from 2020 onwards, in its latest layout, plus Sepang. Outlines are traced from OpenStreetMap survey coordinates - see data/f1-circuits.geojson and build/maps.mjs.

circuits.name: Bahrain International Circuit
circuits.signature: Three heavy braking zones under floodlights, and the only race that starts in daylight and finishes at night.

circuits.name: Jeddah Corniche Circuit
circuits.signature: The fastest street circuit there is: 27 corners, most of them flat, run between walls at an average over 250 km/h.

circuits.name: Albert Park Circuit
circuits.signature: A park road circuit round a lake, resurfaced and widened in 2022 with the old Turn 9-10 chicane taken out.

circuits.name: Shanghai International Circuit
circuits.signature: Drawn from the character shang. Turns 1-3 spiral inwards and tighten all the way, then a 1.2 km back straight into a near-hairpin.

circuits.name: Suzuka International Racing Course
circuits.signature: The only figure-of-eight on the calendar: the back straight crosses over the first sector on a bridge. Esses, Degner, 130R, Casio Triangle.

circuits.name: Miami International Autodrome
circuits.signature: Built around the Hard Rock Stadium. Fast sweeps at both ends, then a slow, awkward chicane section that runs under the freeway.

circuits.name: Autodromo Enzo e Dino Ferrari
circuits.signature: One of only a handful of anti-clockwise circuits, and almost impossible to overtake on. Tamburello, Tosa, Acque Minerali, Rivazza.

circuits.name: Circuit de Monaco
circuits.signature: The shortest and slowest lap of the year. Sainte Devote, the climb to Casino, the Grand Hotel hairpin, the tunnel, the swimming pool.

circuits.name: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuits.signature: Every team's reference track from decades of winter testing. The final chicane was removed in 2023, restoring the flat-out run to the line.

circuits.name: Circuit Gilles Villeneuve
circuits.signature: An island circuit of long straights and slow chicanes, ended by the Wall of Champions on the exit of the last corner.

circuits.name: Red Bull Ring
circuits.signature: Ten corners, three long uphill-downhill straights, and a lap under 65 seconds - the shortest lap time of the season.

circuits.name: Silverstone Circuit
circuits.signature: Home of the first World Championship race. Maggotts-Becketts-Chapel is the fastest sequence of direction changes in the sport.

circuits.name: Circuit de Spa-Francorchamps
circuits.signature: The longest lap of the year, through the Ardennes forest. Eau Rouge-Raidillon blind uphill, then the Kemmel straight; it rains on half the track and not the other.

circuits.name: Hungaroring
circuits.signature: Monaco without the walls: fourteen corners strung together with almost no straight, run in August heat in a natural amphitheatre.

circuits.name: Circuit Zandvoort
circuits.signature: Dune circuit with two banked corners - Hugenholtz at Turn 3 and the 18-degree final banking that fires cars onto the main straight.

circuits.name: Autodromo Nazionale Monza
circuits.signature: The Temple of Speed. Three quarters of the lap is flat out, and the pole time is the fastest average speed of the season.

circuits.name: Madring
circuits.signature: New for 2026, around the IFEMA exhibition grounds: part street, part purpose-built, with a banked corner at La Monumental.

circuits.name: Baku City Circuit
circuits.signature: A 2.2 km flat-out run to the line, and the castle section at Turns 8-9 where the track narrows to 7.6 metres.

circuits.name: Marina Bay Street Circuit
circuits.signature: The original night race, and the most physical of the year. The old Turn 16-19 bay section was replaced by a long straight in 2023.

circuits.name: Circuit of the Americas
circuits.signature: A steep blind climb to the Turn 1 hairpin, an esses sequence borrowed from Maggotts-Becketts, and a long back straight into the Turn 11 hairpin.

circuits.name: Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez
circuits.signature: 2,200 m above sea level, so the air is thin, the cars run maximum downforce and still hit their top speed of the year down the main straight. The lap ends through a baseball stadium.

circuits.name: Autodromo Jose Carlos Pace
circuits.signature: Short, steep and anti-clockwise. The Senna S drops away from the grid and Juncao feeds a long uphill run to the line - which is why the racing is so good here.

circuits.name: Las Vegas Strip Circuit
circuits.signature: A 1.9 km blast down the Las Vegas Boulevard at close to 350 km/h, at a midnight start, in near-freezing desert air.

circuits.name: Lusail International Circuit
circuits.signature: A motorcycle circuit of long, fast, constant-radius sweeps that punish tyres harder than anywhere else on the calendar.

circuits.name: Yas Marina Circuit
circuits.signature: The season finale, run from sunset into the dark. Reprofiled in 2021: the old hairpin became a banked sweep and the marina hotel section was opened out.

circuits.name: Autodromo Internacional do Algarve
circuits.signature: A rollercoaster of blind crests over Algarve hillside, with a downhill final corner onto the main straight. Raced in the pandemic seasons.

circuits.name: Autodromo Internazionale del Mugello
circuits.signature: Ferrari's own test track, used once, for the team's 1000th Grand Prix. A 1.1 km straight and a run of fifth-gear sweeps through Tuscan hills.

circuits.name: Nurburgring
circuits.signature: The modern GP-Strecke, not the Nordschleife alongside it. Used once in 2020 for the Eifel GP, in freezing fog that cancelled two days of running.

circuits.name: Sochi Autodrom
circuits.signature: Laid out through the Olympic Park, defined by the endless 90-degree Turn 3 that wraps around the medals plaza. Dropped from the calendar after 2021.

circuits.name: Istanbul Park
circuits.signature: Home of Turn 8, a quadruple-apex left taken flat that pulls sustained 5g. The 2020 resurface left it so slippery the race was run in effective aquaplaning conditions.

circuits.name: Circuit Paul Ricard
circuits.signature: The blue-and-red striped run-off is the giveaway. The 1.8 km Mistral straight is split by a chicane and ends at the flat-out right of Signes.

circuits.name: Sepang International Circuit
circuits.signature: Two enormous straights joined by a hairpin, with a wide, sweeping first sector. Off the calendar since 2017, and famous for its afternoon monsoons.

geometry: Circuit geometry from OpenStreetMap via https://github.com/bacinger/f1-circuits (MIT).
